text:
jordan-cs: Hey team, customer (acme-corp) reports their Org Admin (alice@acme) was Org Manager pre-merge. After the org merge, when they switch to the project 'payments' the Console shows 'No actions available' and any attempt via the UI to edit roles errors with a 403. API request to GET /v1/projects/payments/permissions returns 403. Repro steps: SSO login -> select org -> select project -> try to manage roles. Anyone seen a merge leave a shadow deny or similar? :thinking:

anna-support: Thanks — can you DM the customer org id and one example user email? Also did they try a logout/login and re-invite? Any browser console stacktrace?

jordan-cs: Sent the org id (org_123) and user email in DM. They did logout/login, and tried re-invite; no change. Browser console shows 403 on the permissions endpoint, payload empty. No CORS errors.

sam-eng: Quick hypothesis: a leftover "deny" policy at org root could shadow lower-level manager grants. During merges we sometimes copy policy blobs and a deny rule can survive. Can you check effective bindings for alice?

jordan-cs: Running a quick audit command I gave them (they're not comfortable running with admin token) so I ran it for them: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_123/effective-bindings?user=alice@acme"
```
Output showed an explicit deny on project-level actions with source: "merged-policy-2026-03".

matt-platform: That matches a known glitch in the org-merge script that copied a deny entry into the resulting org policies. UI will obey effective bindings and hide/deny actions even if the user is Manager at the project. Fix path: remove the deny binding from the policy collection and invalidate the access cache for the org.

anna-support: I'll draft an incident ticket and escalate to policy team. @matt-platform can you remove the deny binding or advise if you want us to do it for the customer?

matt-platform: I can remove the deny binding now. Steps: 1) capture current policy blob 2) PATCH /v1/orgs/org_123/policies with policy minus deny entry 3) trigger cache invalidate: POST /internal/cache/invalidate?org=org_123
I'll perform and post back.

deploy-bot: Job #4521 triggered by matt-platform — policy-patch and cache-invalidate in progress.

matt-platform: Removed deny entry and invalidated caches. Waiting for propagation (~30s).

jordan-cs: Customer reports they can now see actions and the earlier permissions API returns 200. Verified they can edit roles.

anna-support: Marking as resolved. Will add a short postmortem on the merge script to prevent reintroducing deny entries. Follow-up: add a validation step to the merge tooling to reject deny rules unless explicitly approved. :thumbsup:
